newsitem.title: UK: Mideast-Asia VLCC rates hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: Mideast-Asia VLCC rates hit new highs.

text.p: VLCC charter rates posted new highs for Mideast-Asian shipments on Monday bucking the trend seen in most of the rest of the tanker market.
Brokers said demand from Asian refiners helped further buoy the eastbound Middle East VLCC market while returns elsewhere continued to languish at levels disappointing for shipowners.
Three fresh fixtures to South Korea, where crude imports are growing faster than most places, saw rates rising to W77.5-W78.5 on Monday.
And a 250,000 cargo to Japan loading August 28 was fixed at W83.5.
They said shipping availability for VLCCs at the end of August was looking very strengthening the prospects for further gains this week.
"If a charterer needs end-August tonnage they're going to have to pay up," said one broker.
But brokers were wary of predicting how long the higher values might be sustained.
"Back in 1996 the hot market ended during the second week of August and by the end of September rates had fallen from a peak of W80 (Mideast-Japan) to W52.5," said Galbraith's.
VLCC rates for West Africa to Asia also edged higher on Monday to W59.75 for a 245,000 tonne shipment to South Korea.
Other major routed recording slight gains on Monday saw Caribbean/U.S. upcoast 70,000 tonnes recording W122.5 and cross-Mediterranean 80,000 tonnes at W110.
But inter-U.K./Continent returns slipped five points to W95 confirming the weaker trend of last week for Aframax vessels.
